Linux dependency tooling now explains the next monitoring step immediately after
checkbox changes, when switching between VIPM and LVPM, and after a save request.
Accepted requests are clearly distinguished from merged configuration changes;
read-only HEAD checks offer a new-tab link to committed settings without losing
local edits or starting an installation. Uncertain save outcomes retain the
duplicate-request block. LVPM is presented as an optional Linux toolchain without
experimental branding; package-file-only verification and runtime limitations
remain explicit.

Dragon dependency rows separate file presence/parsing from unresolved packages
and expose exact declared names/versions with platform-specific worker evidence.
This UI clarification does not install absent packages, resolve conflicting pins,
or establish runtime success.
